WHEN PLANS CHANGE

Cancellations and refunds policy

Practical rules for changes of plan, cancelled bookings, payment refunds and related credit adjustments. This policy forms part of the Platform Terms when finalised.

Prepared for review · 18 October 2026 · Not yet effective. Business identity, contact details and operational rules require confirmation.

1. Status and the booking agreement2. Details to confirm before paying3. If a couple cancels4. Deposits and advance payments5. Postponements and other changes6. If a supplier cancels or cannot perform7. Weather, emergencies and events beyond control8. How a refund should be recorded9. Commission, fees and credits10. If the parties cannot agree

1. Status and the booking agreement

Review draft dated 18 October 2026. The final policy must name the operator, support route, payment provider and operational refund rules. Read this policy with the Platform Terms, Credit Programme Terms and the supplier agreement accepted for your booking.

A supplier should explain cancellation conditions before a couple accepts or pays. Those conditions can vary with the service, date and work involved, but must be fair and comply with applicable law. This platform policy does not invent a single cancellation percentage for every wedding service.

2. Details to confirm before paying

The booking agreement should identify the service, date, location, supplier, full price, deposit, balance due dates and what is included. It should clearly describe cancellation and postponement terms, any genuinely non-recoverable costs and what happens if the supplier cannot perform.

Keep the quote version you accepted and the supplier’s written confirmations. If a package or starting price does not explain the cancellation position, ask for the complete agreement. A label such as non-refundable is not conclusive where consumer law requires a different result.

3. If a couple cancels

Notify the supplier promptly in the conversation for the relevant booking. Identify the date, invoice or booking reference and whether you are asking to cancel completely or change an element. Do not assume that closing a chat, deleting an account or withholding an instalment cancels a contract.

Ask the supplier to identify the agreed condition relied on and provide a clear breakdown of any retained amount and proposed refund. Depending on the contract and law, relevant circumstances may include work already reasonably performed, costs actually incurred, savings and whether a replacement booking is obtained. No outcome is guaranteed without examining the circumstances.

4. Deposits and advance payments

A deposit can secure a date or fund preparatory work, but should be clearly identified and proportionate to the booking. The agreement should distinguish a deposit from an advance instalment and explain what work or commitment it covers. Suppliers should not retain a payment automatically without considering their agreement and legal obligations.

A couple changing their mind can have different rights from a couple whose supplier fails to deliver the promised service. Any charge must have a lawful, fair basis. Mandatory consumer remedies cannot be waived by a general statement that every payment is non-refundable.

5. Postponements and other changes

If you want to change a date, guest count, location or service scope, ask what alternatives are available and obtain a revised quote or variation in writing. The revised document should address price differences, transfer of payments, new deadlines and cancellation terms.

Neither party should treat an unaccepted variation as binding. If the supplier cannot accommodate a new date, the outcome depends on the original agreement, the reason for the change and applicable law. A replacement supplier must not be substituted without appropriate disclosure and agreement.

6. If a supplier cancels or cannot perform

Suppliers should notify couples promptly when they cannot provide the agreed service, explain the issue and propose an appropriate lawful remedy. Couples should not be required to accept a materially different service or a credit note if a money refund is required.

An alternative service, replacement provider, partial performance or price adjustment may be appropriate only with informed agreement and regard to consumer rights. Keep evidence of what was promised and any additional reasonable costs caused by the failure. WedSparks does not promise to source a replacement or insure those costs.

7. Weather, emergencies and events beyond control

A wedding affected by weather, venue closure, illness, travel restrictions or another serious event needs individual assessment. Check the accepted agreement, the actual effect on performance and applicable law. Describing an event as beyond control does not automatically determine who keeps every payment.

Discuss safe and practical options promptly, including rescheduling or a different scope. Record any agreement and the treatment of money already paid. This draft does not treat every emergency as an automatic full refund or an automatic right for the supplier to retain the whole price.

8. How a refund should be recorded

A proposed refund should specify the booking, invoice, currency, money amount, any credit component, reason and responsible party. Confirm the agreement in writing. Refunds should use the relevant payment-provider process and, where appropriate, the original payment method rather than an unrelated bank account.

Processing and bank timing can vary. The final policy must publish actual refund handling procedures and any reliable service targets; this draft does not invent a guaranteed processing deadline. Never share card passwords, authentication codes or full card details in a refund conversation.

9. Commission, fees and credits

Before payments launch, WedSparks must settle the treatment of its 18% supplier commission and any disclosed processor charges when payments are partially or fully refunded. A couple should receive a clear calculation and must not bear an undisclosed charge or lose a mandatory remedy because of a supplier’s platform fee arrangement.

Refunded qualifying money can affect credit milestones. Refunds of invoices partly funded by credits need a separate record of money and credits restored or adjusted. The final programme rules must address credits already spent fairly and clearly; this draft creates no automatic recovery charge against a couple’s bank account.

10. If the parties cannot agree

Use the Dispute Policy to set out the issue, evidence and requested remedy. An internal review is not a guarantee of a refund and does not replace an external legal or payment-provider right. Be aware that card providers and tribunals can have their own time limits.

Nothing in this policy excludes mandatory Australian or New Zealand consumer protections where they apply. WedSparks must provide its final support details and a clear escalation route before this policy becomes effective.
